headlines.summary: The fund bought $158.6 million of stock, lifting all 69 of its increased positions with no sales.

headlines.title: Altria vs. Philip Morris: Higher Yield or Faster Dividend Growth for Retirees?
headlines.summary: Both tobacco giants beat earnings estimates, raised their dividends, and surged more than 30% this year, but they pull retirees in opposite directions when it comes to income now versus income later.

headlines.title: 5 High-Yield Dividend Stocks That Raised Their Payouts in 2026
headlines.summary: Five income stocks cleared a rare filter this year: every single one raised its dividend payout, even as interest rates punished yield hunters. Find out which names backed those raises with data-center contracts, smoke-free cash flow, and free cash flow that covers the dividend twice over.

headlines.title: Want Income for Life? Philip Morris International Yields 3.2% and Has the Kind of Competitive Moat That Makes the Income Durable.
headlines.summary: A strong legacy business and bright future combine to make Philip Morris a no-brainer for dividend investors.

headlines.title: These 5 Dividend Stocks Raised Their Payouts. Are They Worth Buying in November?
headlines.summary: Five companies quietly raised their dividends in 2026, but a record cash year, a debt-free balance sheet, and a 19-year streak of increases tell very different stories about which payouts can survive the next economic shock.

description: Philip Morris International Inc. operates as a tobacco company. The company offers cigarettes and smoke-free products, including heat-not-burn, e-vapor, and oral nicotine products under the IQOS, VEEV, and ZYN brands; and consumer accessories, such as lighters and matches. It also offers wellness products. The company was incorporated in 1987 and is headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut.
